passage.text: Small shopping streets can be found in many Japanese towns. Some shop owners remember the names and the tastes of their customers, and in this way, they build a friendly relationship with them. However, the number of such shops has been getting smaller in recent years.

illustrations.caption: 商店街。5人が別々の動作（木箱にりんごを並べる店主／レジで支払う女性／紙袋を2つ抱える男性／小犬を散歩させる女の子／店先のメニューを見る年配女性）。
駅の長い階段の下に立つ年配の女性。重い買い物袋を両手に持っている。エスカレーターもエレベーターも無い。吹き出しにホームに立つ姿、赤い斜線。

questions.prompt: Please look at the passage. According to the passage, how do some shop owners build a friendly relationship with their customers?
questions.modelAnswer: By remembering their names and their tastes.

questions.prompt: Now, please look at the people in Picture A. They are doing different things. Tell me as much as you can about what they are doing.
questions.modelAnswer: A shopkeeper is arranging apples in a box. A woman is paying money at a counter. A man is carrying two paper bags. A girl is walking a dog. An older woman is looking at a menu.

questions.prompt: Now, look at the person in Picture B. Please describe the situation.
questions.modelAnswer: The older woman can't get up to the platform because she is holding two heavy bags and there is no escalator.

questions.prompt: Do you think small shops will still be needed in the future?

yes.modelAnswer: Older people cannot always go to large malls. Small shops are close and easy to visit.

no.modelAnswer: Large stores and the Internet are cheaper. People will choose the cheaper way.

questions.prompt: These days, we often see people who need help in the street. Do you often help people who are in trouble?

yes.modelAnswer: I helped a woman carry her bag up the stairs last month. She looked very glad.

no.modelAnswer: I want to help, but I don't know what to say to them. I hope I can do it next time.
